neighbours.label: text about farmland and what it grows (crops, acres, tillage), as opposed to the same frames about industry and buildings
fire: Farmers in the valley grow barley and raise a few sheep.
Most of the district is arable, and the chief crops are oats and potatoes.
The parish has good soil, and the land is chiefly under tillage.
His sons cultivate forty acres of corn on the family farm.
The province produces sugar cane, cotton and tobacco on irrigated land.
Villagers here plant rice in the wet season and keep buffalo.
The estate contains 300 acres, mostly pasture and arable land.
Thanks to new tractors, the profitable cultivation of many acres is possible.
quiet: Workers in the valley build engines and repair a few trucks.
Most of the district is urban, and the chief industries are steel and glass.
The parish has a good school, and the church is chiefly of stone.
His sons manage forty stores of shoes for the family firm.
The province produces steel, cement and chemicals in large factories.
Villagers here sing songs in the wet season and tell stories.
The building contains 300 rooms, mostly offices and meeting halls.
Thanks to new software, the profitable management of many accounts is possible.

notes: The top examples also hold ' what' after 'depending on' or 'no matter', which this label does not cover. Probes on those were 0.10 to 0.24.
